knowledge_point.title: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}9 & -7 & 4 & 7 \\ -6 & -5 & -9 & 8 \\ -2 & 4 & 3 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 3 & 2\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -7 & 25 & 21 \\ -16 & -5 & 6 & 18 \\ 6 & 4 & -9 & -16 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

- $C_{1}:=C_{1}+2C_{2}$
- $C_{3}:=\ldots$
- $C_{4}:=\ldots$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?

explanation: Four choices have absolute pair (3,2); singleton has (2,3) with positive signs. Negate and swap singleton (+2,+3) to (-3,-2), without inspecting matrices.
